text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

It's actually hard to put the bike in the launcher after it is wound without releasing the stored energy.

Man, that was a fun and FAST hour!  I have grandkids and got this for my son and his two kids and whoever else has the stamina to go the distance with them - I have a younger son and daughter-in-law that love to play with their niece and nephew so it's usually one of them.  The only thing is, I had to buy another large container of rechargeable AA batteries.  OMG, these require a total of 28 AA batteries!  And just so you don't run out in the middle of an especially contentious battle, you BETTER have another 28 AA batteries charged and ready...whew, that's a LOT of batteries!  Oh well...better to plan for a fun day than to wimp out, right?  Now when everyone is a bit tuckered out from running around shooting at each other, they can switch to drone strikes with someone flying a drone and another one shooting it down.  Not bad!  I may end up purchasing another set (and whole bunch more batteries) so both my sons, both my daughters-in-law, and my grandkids can play at the same time - big kids and little kids running around, squealing and laughing.  For me, that's better than TV!  I took one star off just for the massive amounts of batteries you need.  Too bad the people who created this didn't think to make these USB rechargeable.

Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink Mix feelings about this product. Had it over a year with minimal travel usage. We usually leave it in our dining room on our kids table so they can do activities while mom cooks. We loved it when it worked but once the batteries died and I replaced the device with new batteries, it turns on and does nothing. It doesn't sense the stylus. It will on a random occasion after multiple attempts say one or two words when pointed on the stylus but then stops again. Changed batteries out a couple of times and unfortunately didn't help. Now, I have two disappointed kids with numerous of these books and told family to get more books for Christmas which will only be to their disappointment that they have no device to use them with.

As for when the device worked, we would loved it and would recommend to any parent with kids under 7. My son is almost 5yo son and 3yo daughter love this. They take turns using it since I only had one of the Leap Start devices but numerous books. My daughter was heart broken after multiple attempts to try new batteries.

I hate to give one start but given the longevity of this product for the price, it needs to last more than a year. I mean one year for a $45 device. Maybe some would say that's worth it but not when you shell out $10 - $15 on each of the books. I might of gotten a faulty device so maybe it's just poor luck on my part.

UPDATE—7/1118
We’ve had our new leapstart book (this time I bought at big box store with a warranty) for 5 months now since the last broke, so far so good but I’m still not sure on longevity still, however i have changed batteries a few times since we use ours alot and have had no issues. I am adding a star as my kids fight over this all the time. I’ve got 6yo boy who LOVES it who is also my reader and 4yo girl who always wants what her brother has but genuinely love this thing. I struggle with getting my kids to play with their $100 toy they got for Christmas but love this thing and it’s a plus for me since it’s educational. So i still can’t give this item as high of a star as I would like because of durability I would recommend it if you don’t care if you have to replace it. I’m glad I did but recommend getting some warranty because after investing in the books and how much my kids like It, you may want to get another.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink

Mattel Games ​Mattel Games PIC FLIP Card Matching Game with 110 Cards in a Decorative Tin, Makes a Great Gift for 7 Year Olds and Up [Amazon Exclusive] My family and I look forward to family game night and Uno has been the game of choice on more than one occasion. It's a fast-paced game that requires luck as much as strategy, and that works well for all of us. We have a couple of Uno variants that we like, and with two adult sons that grew up with Mario games this is a good fit for our family.

This game plays identically to regular Uno in almost every way. It has all of the expected elements of the game - 4 colors, skip, reverse, wild cards and more. However, it also has a special card that changes the game in a fun and often unexpected way, allowing a player to dodge attack cards and send them back to the one who played them. It's powerful enough to change gameplay but not enough to ruin the game.

The cards are decorated with the familiar characters of Mario Brothers games - Bowser, Mario, Luigi, Donkey Kong Jr. and more. Fans of the Mario Brothers franchise will like this deck.

The game is packed nicely in a metal tin that protects the cards and keeps them together.

I am not the least bit unhappy with this game and my family and I have been enjoying it. We look forward to game nights and this game will be a part of those nights.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games ​Mattel Games PIC FLIP Card Matching Game with 110 Cards in a Decorative Tin, Makes a Great Gift for 7 Year Olds and Up [Amazon Exclusive]

text_fidelity_a:
LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship) When I got this, I still didn't solve the Rubik's cube. I know there are all kinds of tutorials, but I wanted to solve it on my own. Fast-forward 11 years later, I flipped the table (so to speak) and watched a couple tutorials. This was the cube I used to solve the puzzle for the first time. I watched a couple videos of the cube before receiving mine to get a better understanding of the mechanisms and design. During my first session, I set the magnets to the strongest and left the dials as they were. Two hours is how long it took me to solve it on the first try.

I like that this cube comes with a handful of accessories. I use the case to carry the cube with me to and from work. It stays on my desk; whenever I have to read something on my monitors and not use the keyboard, I solve a little bit. Now I can solve the cube in minutes, though it took me a few days to get to this point. I now have the spring and tension set to the strongest for how much force can be pulled and weakest for how fast turns can be. (Apologies for not using the correct terms, but I tried looking up what the dials exactly do and I still can't figure out which does what with regard to the terminology, but I base it off feel.)

The cube comes with a leather bag and a tool to adjust the magnets. The first time I accessed the dials, I used a pen to pop off the tiles. They can be difficult to pull off by hand alone, even after being pulled so many times. The lever for each dial also was difficult to pull. Now, I leave it semi-flush to the dial to make it easier to access in the future. They also pop off easily, but are [somewhat] easy to put back. The magnet levels sometimes move on their own. If I happen to notice a magnet at a strength I didn't set it at, I'll re-adjust. Annoying, but an easy fix. I no longer use the tool that came with the cube because any item small and flat enough will work. The bag is kept in the box for now.

There are two manuals that come with the cube: one for the cube itself and the other on how to solve it. I tried using the solve tutorial but found it confusing with some typographical errors, so I used videos. I learn better visually anyway. Even though the cube's manual has great illustrations for the mechanics, I failed to understand what they actually do, so I looked up videos for that too.

This is the third cube I own and currently it's my favorite. Each time my time lowers after solving, I adjust the settings. I'm becoming a speedcuber without realizing it.
text_fidelity_b: LiangCuber Tornado V3 M Flagship Speed Cube QY Toys X Man Tornado V3 Magnetic 3x3 Cube (Tornado V3 M Magnetic Core Flagship)

HOT WHEELS IRON MAN REPULSOR BLAST LAUNCHER Kid enjoys it, but it's not the thrilling launch you were expecting.
The packaging on this Iron Man Hotwheels launcher is eye-catching - the type of thing your child would be immediately drawn to. My 4.5 yo has been pining for this item ever since he caught a glimpse. The toy was easy to remove from the packaging, something we can all rejoice over. The instructions are straightforward, but it was unclear to me if the toy needs to "click in" to be launched or if it is simply placed on the track inside the larger car (the launcher). The mask doesn't close all the way if you click it in, which tells me it's not really meant to be there. I was expecting more of a spring action launch, but it's really just a result of the handle shooting it forward. The results are hit and miss.

As an adult, I found the movement needed to pull back the mask for loading to be slightly awkward (it's a slight lifting motion on a very small tab). My 4.5 yo managed to do it no problem: smaller fingers I suppose. I also found the launching slightly difficult as you need to hold onto the larger vehicle with one hand while pulling back and releasing the handle with enough force to *actually* launch the car. My child thinks any amount of launching is thrilling and doesn't seem to mind that the car sometimes barely leaves the launcher, so I suppose it's fine.

The larger car does have fittings to connect with a track, so that may be helpful (we don't own any HotWheels tracks).

All-in-all, your little Iron Man fan will likely be delighted by this. The adults in your house may not be.
text_fidelity_b: HOT WHEELS IRON MAN REPULSOR BLAST LAUNCHER

Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show is a fun way for your little fashion diva to spend some free time. All you do is download the application on your smartphone, tablet, or iPod touch, draw some fashion designs, and then scan them. Your fashion will then show up on an actual fashion model, in 3D, to your child’s delight.

My girls are fashion designers in the making so I knew they would love playing with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show. It takes little effort to get going. You just add the application to your smartphone or tablet, and then have your child start drawing. Once scanned through the application, kids will be able to see their own fashion design on an actual model. This caused squeals of satisfaction from my girls who loved seeing their fashion on screen.

From my children’s perspectives, there is little that isn’t perfect with a toy like this, but as an adult, I can see a few issues. One has already been stated by others who have used the device, but bears repeating: The phone or tablet you use will make a difference. Not all smartphones or tablets are created equally and the colors may look a little off. If you have more than one device and it doesn’t look good on one, then you might want to consider downloading the application to another device. It could make a difference and it’s simple enough to do.

The included accessories with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show are a little limited. The small colored pencils are also somewhat of an obstacle, as they are not good for larger hands. But overall, this is a fun fashion design kit and I cannot imagine a fashion- loving child who wouldn’t fall in love with it.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show

text_fidelity_a:
UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid This horse is striking in appearance. It looks wild and spirited. It is quite a conversation piece on its looks alone. I would give it five stars alone for that. Movement is not as spectacular, but it does move. There’s a winding key and start/stop control levers. The horse is not able to take more than 5 steps without halting or simply falling over. It looks like the last motions of a horse before succumbing to the effects of a trank dart. The kit is a real bear to assemble. The instructions must be heeded. You may find you have to flip ahead a few pages at times to see just what this subassembly is that you are working on and where it is supposed to go. I knew at the start that I would need to sand the pieces and use the provided wax. Ther's not a whole lot of wax. It’s a 1 inch slice of a candle but the important thing is that it enough for the horse. The wax is somewhat soft, like beeswax. I had no problem with missing pieces. There are six boards with laser cut parts. If you don't see anything missing, you have all the parts. Assembly is a bit tedious and somewhat painful. As the model continues to take shape and become more horse-like there is the adrenalin surge all model builders feel when they are nearing the end. Once assembly is completed the key is wound and switch is moved. My model just sat there. C’mon little horsy, let’s go. Well, back-winding the key overcomes the initial friction and horse begins to haltingly show movement. Lots of going back and forth with the key helps to distribute the wax and the horse becomes more limber. After lots of massaging like this you can get the horse to take 4 or maybe 5 steps. Max is 9 and only rarely achieved. It will usually fall over to announce it is finished walking. Well and good. It is still a cool model and I would build one again. I’m giving it 5 stars but 4 would be reasonable too. I wish it walked a bit better and that the instructions had a bit of expository text. This is a worthwhile model that will occupy 8 hours of your life in assembly. It is ingenious.

I have a few hints on this horse:
Mine locked up once while fully wound up. I could not get it to operate at all. I tried moving the legs and rapping the body with my knuckles. Nothing! My horse was dead. It was not until I grasped the horses neck and moved it forward and back that the gears unlocked. This only happened once, but it was super frustrating as I was contemplating opening up the entire model to fix it.

Understand at the outset that this horse can’t walk for long. If you watch the clever videos the horse appears to leave its stall and seems to be on a journey to a pasture or whatever. If you look closely the horse only takes a few steps in each scene. Clever editing makes it look like the horse can go on a pastoral journey. Not really complaining because all the ad copy and literature says the horse can’t go far. This is only a problem if your expectations are too high and unrealistic. It is what it is, a model of mechanical horse. So enjoy that as I do I.

My rubber band broke. I suppose it had a nick in it that grew over time. I was able to cut out the broken piece and retie the rubber band but it is not easy working in the body of the assembled model. So do examine the length of the rubber band before assembly.

Update on the rubber band issue 5 days later:
The rubber band broke again. No, I haven’t over wound it. I’ll have to see if I can get a replacement from somewhere.

The rubber bands for the horse’s mane and tail are genius. Looks great and the bands lie perfectly when cut. I was worried I’d need hair styling skills to make the horse look good. It was no problem.

Seriously, sand everything. Knock down the edges of the large pieces as well so they lose their painful sharpness. If you have to reach into the interior of the model later you will be glad you did.

Some parts are seeming impossible to press together with human hands. I finally resorted to a small furniture clamp with soft jaws to supplement my finger strength. I think pliers or small c-clamp would work, as well.

A cushiony work surface was helpful in supporting a board while I was breaking a part loose from the board. I used towel I use for assembly projects.

It really takes 8 uninterrupted hours to assemble this model no matter how skilled you think you are. If you leave out trying to be extra careful and the extra sanding I guess you could do it in about five.

On page 13 of the instructions I was confused. The diagram seems to suggest that the rubber band should be folded upon itself in thirds. After puzzling on this I covinced myself that doubling the band was correct and it turned out to be right choice.

Check for proper operation of parts during assembly. In some steps you are "told" to operate the key and check that the parts move freely. This is very important. Once the horse is fully assembled getting back inside it is a difficult task since gear timing must be maintained.

There is a down side to using the wax. Your hands will get a coating of wax and when that is transferred to the horse there will be discolored spots. Try to keep the wax from where you don't want the wood to darken. I washed my hands frequently and still ended up with a horse that is more pinto than wood white.

There are no troubleshooting hints in the instructions. If you can't find help on the website you are on your own. I do have a vibe from Ugears that they are helpful and I think you can correspond with them and get help if you have a bad problem.

The actual concepts focused in this activity book are great, but there are two areas of improvement outside of the lessons:

The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.

text_fidelity_a:
KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S) This is yet another variation of the "Boogie Board" drawing tablet. If you are not familiar with the concept, it is NOT a digital tablet, but essentially a reusable drawing tool much like a whiteboard. It starts off as an opaque black surface that reveals a different color underneath with pressure. So you can draw on it using the included pen, a fingernail, or anything with enough pressure really, and then erase it all at once with the erase button on the bottom. The only electronics involved is a battery that "zaps" the display back to opaque to start over. This battery should last years as it only gets used when erasing for a split second.
I actually like this one better than some of our other ones as the contrast between the black and revealed color is quite high. Some of the inexpensive Boogie Board clones lack contrast and can be hard to see sometimes, but that is not the case here. It also seems to have a multi-colored background, so as you draw or write, it feels like the color is changing (really it is just revealing a different part of the material behind the LCD). I also really like the size of it, as our other drawing tablets were small whereas this one feels closer to a sheet of paper. My 12 year old son actually finds this comfortable for using as a scratch pad for his math homework, which is a great environmentally friendly alternative to scrap paper. And my younger kids like drawing pictures on it or playing games like tick-tack-toe.
You do have to be a little bit careful about resting your hand on it as it seems even that amount of pressure will leave a mark, and sadly you can't erase part of a picture, you can only erase the entire thing in one shot with the button. But this is true of all similar drawing pads due to how it works, so that is no fault of this product. As far as the Boogie Board clones go, this is my favorite so far.
text_fidelity_b: KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S)

text_fidelity_a: Schleich Horse Club, 15-Piece Playset, Horse Toys for Girls and Boys 5-12 years old Pick Up with Horse Box This is a really cute set good sized set (roughly 18 inches long and 4 inches high) made of rugged plastic and with real rubber tires.  The truck looks realistic with nice details inside the cab with a center console, two bucket seats, a dashboard and a steering wheel.  It is molded in 4 colors plus a clear plastic windshield, sunroof and back window.  The side doors have no windows.  The steering wheel turns, but is not functional for turning the wheels.  The two front doors of the truck both open.  The hood of the truck opens to reveal an engine.  Nice detail including non-functioning headlights, parking lights, front grill, side mirrors, gas cap and a rear tailgate that also opens.  The only assembly required on the truck is putting on the 4 tires, which should be easy for just about any kid.  The horse trailer also requires putting on 4 tires and a special wheel in the front; also there are 6 trailer pieces that have to be snapped in place. An illustrated book shows how to install the pieces.  Pretty easy, but a younger child might have a little trouble figuring it out.  The pictures on the side of the trailer and the license plates on the truck and trailer are provided in a sheet of stickers, which a child can place where they like.  Includes a completely black horse with a blanket, 2 figures (a driver for the truck and a handler for the horse) and several accessories for the horse including a bridle, halter, saddle, a couple brushes, a bale of hay and a bunch of carrots.  Suitable for both boys or girls, especially those who like horses.  Probably this toy would be preferred by girls since the truck is pink and the horse handler is female. Even some adult collectors might like this set as it is colorful, detailed and well made. The real downside that I see to this set is that if you have very young children who will be around this, they could easily put one of the small pieces in their mouth and choke.  There is no instructions on showing how to use the horse accessories; most are obvious, but a couple are not.  The most important thing to know is that this is more of an "old school" type of toy; no batteries, no motors, no remotes.  A lot of kids today want the latest electronic devices and radio controlled toys, but this toy allows them to use their imaginations a little. I think that's a plus, but if you buy this for the kid who wants a cell phone instead, there will be a level of disappointment, I'm sure.  Note that this is made by a German company, with components from Germany, China, Romania and Tunisia. It's not that important to me where it is made, but it might be to you.  Note too that you can also buy other items in this series, such as a barn type structure, a corral and other horses.  If your child insists on other components, it could get expensive, if you give in.  As a kid at heart, I like this toy a lot myself and would keep it if I didn't have so many other things.  It will probably go to a grandson.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Horse Club, 15-Piece Playset, Horse Toys for Girls and Boys 5-12 years old Pick Up with Horse Box

Cons:
*The two included trucks are not of equal quality, one is weightier and more metal the other is cheap mostly yellow plastic. You would think they'd have similar trucks since it is head to head.

Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel) I've seen these decorative bookends before, but they're rather pricey. So when I saw one that wasn't as expensive and looked like it would be a fun project, I decided to give it a try. I've always enjoyed crafts and a recent project was assembling and decorating an entire dollhouse.
That project, which took a couple of months, was nowhere near as frustrating as this, which took two days (when I'm determined, I'm determined).
Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ We absolutely love our dinosaurs, dragons, and lifelike statues of real animals from this brand, and this extra-large dinosaur is no exception. The thing you should know about these is that they are a very hard resin like material. This makes them much better for children who are old enough to use the statues responsibly and not bash them on things such as their little sister, because they are very hard and heavy and have absolutely no give to them. On this particular model, the end of the tail is the most dangerous part aside from the sheer size and weight of the overall piece.

This dinosaur is much larger than the cheapo dinosaurs that you get in multi-packs that are made in China, and the level of craftsmanship and detail here is sufficient for even the most exacting dinosaur connoisseur. That said, though the description talks about scoop shaped teeth being a major part of what makes this dinosaur cool, I was unable to really discern much scoop detail on the teeth, given the relative size of the teeth versus the relative size of the dinosaur. Just something to be aware of. But that's not me complaining about the level of detail.

I love the artistic detailing on the hide, the bluish bumps on the back, the little spines, and the huge amount of expression in the face. My toddler son is just beginning a dinosaur phase and enjoyed stomping this large dinosaur through his truck collection and roaring with great feeling. I think that as his knowledge of dinosaurs expands, so will his appreciation of all the small differentiating details that give this dinosaur personality, character, and most importantly, accuracy.

As long as you are aware of the hard and heavy resin material used to create these, you will be deeply impressed by the detailing, durability, and potential for imaginative play inherent in the figure.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+
